issues.legal_issue: Statutory solatium is not payable on compensation awarded for temporary occupation of land.
material_facts: The land was occupied temporarily for the purpose of an event, and possession was taken for several months.
The owner’s title remained with the owner during the occupation.
Compensation was determined in a proceeding for temporary occupation and was intended to compensate actual loss, rather than to reflect market value.
The High Court enhanced compensation but refused to award statutory solatium.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to statutory solatium on compensation determined for temporary occupation; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, does not apply to compensation under Section 35. Temporary occupation under Part VI is distinct from acquisition under Part II because occupation takes possession without extinguishing title, whereas acquisition vests the property in the State. Section 23(2) relates to market value under the first clause of Section 23(1); it does not apply to compensation for actual loss under Section 35, nor to damage under the second clause of Section 23(1). The Court relied on Tan Bug Taim v. Collector of Bombay, AIR 1946 Bom. 216.

predicates.temporary_occupation_compensation_procee: The proceeding concerns compensation for land occupied temporarily.
predicates.possession_taken_without_title_transfer: The occupier took possession while the owner retained title to the land.
predicates.compensation_based_on_actual_loss_not_ma: The compensation was intended to compensate actual loss and was not based on the land’s market value.

issues.definition: When a temporary-occupation compensation proceeding involves possession without transfer of title and compensation for actual loss rather than market value, statutory solatium is not awarded.
